output.brief: The evidence points mainly at the scholarship cut, not the Admissions Office. Yield fell only in the tiers whose awards were reduced: Dean's from 45.2% to 31.9%, and Merit from 44.9% to 32.3%. Presidential awards were unchanged and yield held at about 36%. The no-award group barely moved, from 38.5% to 37.0%. Applications, admits and GPA all rose, so the applicant pool wasn't the problem. Early-action decisions went out on time on the old system, yet their yield fell about as much as regular decision (7.4 points against 7.5). That undercuts the idea that the slow portal rollout caused the drop. The slow rollout was real and probably cost some individual students, such as the one in the counsellor's email. I can't size that effect, and I can't say whether the frozen reader posts or the late scoring module caused the delay. I'm fairly confident, around 80%, about the scholarship finding. Don't replace the director on this evidence. Take the scholarship schedule back to the finance committee, with the net-revenue trade-off modelled for the tiers where yield fell, before award letters go out. Also set a turnaround target for regular decision. Hold off on ordering the vendor to rebuild the upload module until there's proof that documents were actually lost.
